newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian govt opens talks on bank layoffs.
newsitem.headline: Italian govt opens talks on bank layoffs.

text.p: Italy's centre-left government on Wednesday began talks with banking association ABI and union leaders on how to defuse a crisis over planned lay-offs throughout the sector.
Cabinet undersecretary Enrico Micheli and Labour Minister Tiziano Treu were meeting ABI and union representatives separately at the government's offices.

Francesca Santoro, a senior member of Italy's biggest trades union confederation Cgil, was cautiously optimistic on her way into talks, but said: "We have to listen to what the government says about how the meeting with ABI went."
Staff at the Banca di Roma group went on strike on Tuesday in protest at more than 4,000 planned layoffs at the group.

Analysts say the problem is sector-wide, and that huge overstaffing must be addressed and radical restructuring implemented if the Italian banking sector is to achieve the sort of profitability seen elsewhere in Europe.
